# Offline JMdict English and JMnedict

Yomoku uses EDRDG's Japanese/English word dictionary and Japanese names dictionary.
Source data and the derived index are **CC BY-SA 4.0**; Yomoku code remains MIT.
See [attribution](ATTRIBUTION.txt), the complete [EDRDG statement](edrdg-licence.html)
and [CC legal code](CC-BY-SA-4.0.txt). These notices and complete project documents
are copied beside every prepared index and bundled in Android assets. Settings
exposes the complete attribution, legal code and project documentation offline.
Definitions are not yet connected to the word panel.

## Pinned sources

[sources.lock.json](sources.lock.json) pins both official daily XML snapshots
created **2026-10-25**, their compressed SHA-256 and raw entry counts:

| Source | Entries | Official download |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| JMdict English (`JMdict_e.gz`) | 218,957 | https://www.edrdg.org/pub/Nihongo/JMdict_e.gz |
| JMnedict (`JMnedict.xml.gz`) | 743,682 | https://www.edrdg.org/pub/Nihongo/JMnedict.xml.gz |

Use English JMdict, including its overlapping name entries, rather than JMdict_b
which removes names. This permits independent word and name matches. These are
the standard XML distributions, not the separately published NG format.

## Prepare and verify

Python 3.11+ and its bundled SQLite suffice; no third-party Python dependencies.
Commands run at the repository root:

```sh
# Entirely offline; supply the exact compressed source files in this directory.
python3 tools/prepare-dictionaries.py --sources .local/dictionaries/upstream
# Explicit network opt-in if the pinned versions are still served upstream.
python3 tools/prepare-dictionaries.py --download
# Eight synthetic tests, with the real-data test explicitly skipped.
python3 -W error tools/test-prepare-dictionaries.py -v
# Nine tests including both complete pinned dictionaries.
python3 -W error tools/test-prepare-dictionaries.py --full .local/dictionaries/index-v1-20261025 -v
# Second independent build; every bundle byte should match with the same toolchain.
python3 tools/prepare-dictionaries.py --output .local/dictionaries/index-v1-20261025-repeat
diff -r .local/dictionaries/index-v1-20261025 .local/dictionaries/index-v1-20261025-repeat
# Inspect all exact-form candidates, preserving separate sources and restrictions.
python3 tools/prepare-dictionaries.py --lookup 東京
```

All generated bytes stay in ignored `.local/dictionaries/`. A published directory
contains `dictionary.sqlite3`, `build.json`, `sources.lock.json`, complete `notices/`
and exact compressed `upstream/` inputs for future offline reproduction. The tool
copies and hashes inputs **before XML parsing**. It verifies creation dates/counts,
foreign keys and database integrity; builds transactionally in a temporary sibling;
and publishes by directory rename only after success. Published files are read-only.
Existing output is reused only when every file matches; changed/corrupt input never
overwrites it. Use a fresh versioned output directory for a reviewed update.

`build.json` records Python/SQLite versions, compiler SHA-256 and all generated
file checksums. Binary reproducibility requires the same compiler, input bytes,
Python and SQLite versions. Verified host baseline: Python 3.14.8, SQLite 3.51.2;
index size **279,109,632 bytes**, SHA-256
`0be9d4493aa3fa4474dbb27291820a63a27748dbc63e5517f67be39ffea8e152`.
The complete uncompressed preparation bundle is about 288 MiB; no Android asset
size, extraction time or lookup performance measurement is claimed.

## Index contract (version 1)

This is an independent immutable asset, not a migration of the user's database.
SQLite `application_id = 0x594f4449` and `user_version = 1` identify it.

- `metadata(key, value)` stores canonical JSON source provenance.
- `entries(source, entry_id, payload)` uses the source's stable `ent_seq` within
  each dictionary. IDs can overlap across sources. `payload` is canonical UTF-8
  JSON; senses, glosses, readings and translations keep original order.
- `forms(surface, source, entry_id)` indexes every exact written/reading form with
  BINARY collation. Its composite primary key supports indexed candidate lookup.
  Lookup binds parameters and returns all matching entries ordered by source/ID.
  There is no Unicode normalization, fuzzy matching or invented definition.

Payloads contain `kanji`/`readings` objects with `text` and optional upstream
`ke_inf`, `ke_pri`, `re_restr`, `re_inf`, `re_pri` lists. `no_kanji: true` retains
`re_nokanji`. Word `senses` retain optional `stagk`, `stagr`, `pos`, `field`, `misc`,
`s_inf`, `dial`, `xref`, `ant` lists, plus `glosses` and optional `loan_sources`.
Glosses retain `text`, `lang`, optional `g_type` and `g_gend`; loan sources retain
`text`, `lang`, `type`, `wasei`. Name `names` groups retain `name_type`, `xref`
and ordered `translations`. Translation records use the gloss record shape.
Only English glosses/name translations survive; loan-source languages are metadata.
Missing language defaults to `eng`, as in the source DTDs. Empty optional lists
are omitted. Unknown XML structures fail instead of silently losing new fields.

XML entities expand to upstream human-readable labels. An omitted word POS inherits
the previous sense's POS within that entry, including across non-English senses.
Spelling/reading and sense restrictions remain explicit: exact index matches are
**candidates**, not permission to show every restricted sense for every spelling.
Rust lookup is implemented by `yomoku-storage::dictionary::Dictionary`; pure typed
payloads and restriction rules live in `yomoku-core::dictionary`. The independent
read-only connection validates format identity, binds exact surface/base forms,
unions/deduplicates source-scoped entries and retains both query provenances.
It returns complete raw payloads alongside applicable spelling/reading/sense
indices. Display only those applicable views: raw payloads can contain senses
restricted to other spellings/readings. All appropriate readings survive; the
analyzer's single reading never filters homophones. No normalization/fuzzy lookup,
vocabulary mutation occurs. The selected-reader-word repository separately counts
exact-surface lifetime encounters in a user-state read transaction. Lazy FIFO/typed
JNI carries complete word/name candidates and count; UI and compact POS remain next.
The index repository checks format identity, not cryptographic integrity; the installer verifies the
manifest/checksum before supplying a published immutable path.

## Android assets and private installation

After preparing the exact index above, Gradle's `bundleDictionaries` runs
`python3 tools/bundle-dictionaries.py` offline. [android.lock.json](android.lock.json)
pins the complete build manifest plus the index size/hash. Every copied file is
verified before the asset directory is published; changed/corrupt inputs leave
existing output intact. Reviewed data updates require a fresh generated output.
The APK includes the immutable index, build/source manifests, all notices, exact
compressed XML inputs and exact compiler for future reproduction with this repo.
The APK uses `upstream/*.gz.bin` names to prevent Android's asset merger from
expanding `.gz` inputs. Remove only the final `.bin` when recovering source files;
their original compressed bytes still match `build.json` and `sources.lock.json`.
No generated dictionary bytes are committed to Git.

`wordDictionaryFiles(context)` is lazy and worker-only. Its `verifiedPath()`
rehashes cached bytes, or stages/fsyncs/checks size and SHA-256 before atomic
publication into private no-backup storage. The content-addressed `.sqlite3` file
is read-only. Corrupt/unsafe cache repair replaces the inode, preserving held
readers; interrupted staging is discarded on retry. Never open published inodes
for writing. NativeBridge's worker-only verified_word_dictionary_path callback
supplies this verified path to the FIFO. The worker reuses a read-only connection;
failed dictionary queries retire it so explicit retry reopens a repaired inode.
Library, Settings, reader opening and token/status reads do not extract the index.

The raw index is 279,109,632 bytes; the APK also retains both compressed XML
inputs. Installed APK size/extraction results belong in `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`.
No physical arm64 or lookup performance claim is made.

```sh
python3 -W error tools/test-bundle-dictionaries.py -v
python3 tools/bundle-dictionaries.py
```

Rust checks (run from the repository root; the data path must be absolute because
Cargo runs tests from the package directory):

```sh
cargo test -p yomoku-core --test dictionary --all-features --locked --offline
cargo test -p yomoku-storage dictionary --locked --offline
YOMOKU_DICTIONARY_INDEX="$PWD/.local/dictionaries/index-v1-20261025/dictionary.sqlite3" cargo test -p yomoku-storage full_index_all --locked --offline -- --ignored
```

The regular checks require no downloaded data. The explicitly ignored full-index
test decodes/validates every real payload and checks 食べた→食べる, kana, simultaneous
東京 word/name results and no match. No lookup-performance or APK-size claim.

## Updates and evidence

Official downloads roll daily. The tool rejects a newer snapshot at an unchanged
URL; never disable checksum verification. Retain the prepared `upstream/` files
or distribute them with the derived CC BY-SA index for offline reproduction.
For each data refresh, download both official inputs to a new directory, inspect
their creation comments/embedded DTDs, review format/licence changes, update lock
checksums/counts, attribution date/hash and output version, then run synthetic/full
fixtures and the independent rebuild comparison. Review freshness before each app
release; this is a build-time update process, without adding in-app network access.

Primary documentation verified 2026-10-25:

- https://www.edrdg.org/edrdg/licence.html (current V4.0 terms, app attribution,
  documentation inclusion and update procedure)
- https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project.html
- https://www.edrdg.org/enamdict/enamdict_doc.html
- https://www.edrdg.org/pub/Nihongo/ (daily editions; English versus basic/NG)
- Each pinned archive's embedded DTD (restrictions, POS inheritance, language defaults)
- https://docs.python.org/3/library/xml.etree.elementtree.html (streaming parser;
  processed entry nodes removed from the root to bound memory)

Local project HTML copies retain upstream bytes, including historical wording;
the current EDRDG licence statement supplies the V4.0 terms. The old `/wiki/index.php/`
URL now returns a wiki-closure notice, so the complete static `.html` project page
is retained instead.
